questions.q: The length of the latus rectum of the ellipse 3x² + y² = 12 is —
questions.work:
x²/4 + y²/12 = 1: major axis along y, a² = 12, b² = 4.
LR = 2b²/a = 2·4/√12 = 8/(2√3) = 4/√3.

questions.q: The parabola with vertex (−3, 0) and directrix x + 5 = 0 is —
questions.work:
Vertex to directrix: −3 − (−5) = 2 = a, opening to the right.
(y − 0)² = 4·2(x + 3) = 8(x + 3).

questions.q: For the ellipse 16x² + y² = 16 find: (a) the length of the major axis; (b) the length of the minor axis; (c) the eccentricity; (d) the foci.
questions.answer:
x²/1 + y²/16 = 1: major axis along y, a = 4, b = 1.
(a) 2a = 8. (b) 2b = 2.
(c) e² = 1 − 1/16 = 15/16 ⇒ e = √15/4.
(d) c = ae = √15 ⇒ foci (0, ±√15). (Latus rectum 2b²/a = ½; directrices y = ±16/√15.)

questions.answer:
a = 6, c = ae = 10 ⇒ b² = 100 − 36 = 64.
Vertices on the y-axis: y²/36 − x²/64 = 1.

For the ellipse 3x² + 2y² = 6 find the lengths of the axes, the foci, the vertices and the eccentricity.
questions.answer:
x²/2 + y²/3 = 1: major axis along y, a² = 3, b² = 2.
Major axis 2√3, minor axis 2√2.
c² = 3 − 2 = 1 ⇒ foci (0, ±1); vertices (0, ±√3); e = c/a = 1/√3.
